Ants exhibit fixed action patterns, exemplified by circular motion without leadership, indicating no feedback-based modification. In contrast, humans retain juvenile traits into adulthood, prolonging developmental stages and enabling lifelong learning. This biological immaturity underpins societal structures where education spans decades. The core duality lies between deterministic behavior (ants) and probabilistic adaptation (humans), modeled mathematically through feedback loops and state transition matrices. Failure modes include behavioral rigidity in ants and cognitive stagnation in humans lacking feedback.
